What it caught

A plaintext Python SSH worm from my Threat Harbour honeypot that recruits VPS hosts into a Komari-based botnet. Read the analysis of bendi.py

Defensive takeaways

  1. Blocklist these passwords

    Deny-list the top 10 in your IdP; require manager-generated secrets.

  2. Expect recon, not intrusion

    Mostly uname/hostname/whoami in 2.28s sessions — alert on discovery bursts, not single logins.

  3. Watch persistence paths

    Writes toward authorized_keys keep recurring — alert on any unexpected one.

How it works

  • Daily GitHub Actions pipeline parses Cowrie logs on-box, commits aggregates only
  • Grafana + Loki + Promtail monitor stack, localhost-bound via SSH tunnel
  • Reproducible offline analysis in scripts/ with full methodology docs

Parsed Cowrie JSONL on sensor with Python json parser (same source Promtail ships to Loki). Aggregates only; raw IPs and payloads not published.

Aggregates are published daily; the full dataset ships alongside as data.json.

One VM, one IP, one region — what hit this sensor, not the internet. Never attribution.
